provenance.authored_by: claude (investigation session), from blind-judge critiques of opus specs; guards calibrated live on five flag requests

match: Add a command-line flag to an existing tool or script that makes it print extra diagnostic, trace, debug or progress information

fit.q: Does the request add a new command-line flag or option to an existing tool or script?
Is the purpose of the new flag to make the tool print extra information about what it is doing?

requires.q: Is the file described in `target.usage` a library that other scripts load, rather than a command people run directly?

escalate.q: To add the new flag well, does an engineer first need to understand branching or fallback logic inside the tool?

tool.q: Which candidate names the existing tool or script that gets the new flag?

flag.q: Which candidate is the new flag, exactly as it should be typed?

reported.q: Which single word names the things the new flag reports on?

items.text: Add `{flag}` to `{tool}` so that it {desired}.
`{tool_path}`: {tool_summary}. It has no `{flag}` option today.
`{tool_path}`: {tool_summary}. The text `{flag}` already appears in it; find out what it does today before adding anything.
`{tool} {flag}` {desired}; without `{flag}` the output and exit codes are unchanged.
Before editing, read `{tool_path}` end to end and list every place the flag must report on, including ones inside helpers, loops and command substitutions.

guards.q: Does the new flag report on fixed checks or steps written in the code, each of which runs or is skipped?

items.text: Before editing, trace every path through `{tool_path}` that makes an attempt the flag must report, including retries, fallbacks and early exits, so that no attempt goes unreported.

guards.q: Does the new flag report on a sequence of attempts, where each attempt can succeed or fail?

items.text: Choose one design and commit to it: a single logging helper called at each reporting point (preferred when the points are scattered), or wrapping an existing helper those points already share. Criteria: every point covered, smallest diff, default output untouched.
`{tool} {flag}` {desired}.
Without `{flag}`, the standard output and exit codes of `{tool}` are identical to today's.
Diagnostic output from `{flag}` goes to stderr only, so anything that consumes stdout is unaffected.
Each diagnostic line has a stable, greppable prefix and shape: `[{tool_name}] <event> <subject> -> <result>`.
Report what did not happen as well as what did: results are `hit`, `miss`, or `skipped (<reason>)`, so "not checked" is distinguishable from "checked and absent".

guards.q: Is each thing the new flag reports on a lookup or check that either finds something or comes up empty?
Does the new flag report on a sequence of attempts, where each attempt can succeed or fail?

items.text: Each attempt is reported in order with what was tried and how it ended (for example `ok`, `retry (<reason>)`, `limit (<reason>)`, `error (<exit code>)`), including attempts that were skipped.

guards.q: Does the new flag report on a sequence of attempts, where each attempt can succeed or fail?

items.text: Finish with one summary line on stderr giving the totals: how many {reported} were reported and how each ended.
`{flag}` is accepted before or after the positional arguments.

guards.q: Does the tool described in `target.usage` take positional (non-flag) arguments?

items.text: `{flag}` can appear anywhere among the existing options.

guards.q: Does the tool described in `target.usage` take positional (non-flag) arguments?

items.text: `{flag}` is listed in the usage/help text in the existing format, with a one-line description.

items.output: stderr has one `[{tool_name}]` line for each of the {reported}, then the summary line; stdout is unchanged
items.reasoning: Diagnostics are the feature; keeping them off stdout protects every consumer of the normal output.

items.input: a run of `{tool}` with `{flag}` where one of the {reported} cannot run
items.reasoning: Something that never ran must still be visible, or users cannot tell "not checked" from "absent".

guards.q: Does the new flag report on fixed checks or steps written in the code, each of which runs or is skipped?

items.output: no `[{tool_name}]` lines on stderr; stdout and the exit code identical to before the change
items.reasoning: The default path must not change at all.

items.input: a run with `{flag}` where the first attempt fails and a later one succeeds
items.output: stderr shows one line per attempt, in order, each with its outcome, then the summary; stdout carries the normal result
items.reasoning: The trace exists to explain what happened across attempts, including the failures that were recovered from.

guards.q: Does the new flag report on a sequence of attempts, where each attempt can succeed or fail?

items.text: `diff <({runner} {tool_path} 2>/dev/null) <({runner} {tool_path} {flag} 2>/dev/null)` produces no output.

Does the tool described in `target.usage` read its input from standard input when no file argument is given?

items.text: `{runner} {tool_path} {flag} 2>&1 >/dev/null` prints one or more `[{tool_name}]` lines and the summary line.

Does the tool described in `target.usage` read its input from standard input when no file argument is given?

items.text: `{runner} {tool_path} 2>&1 >/dev/null` prints no `[{tool_name}]` lines.

items.text: Pipe the same small valid input into `{runner} {tool_path}` once with and once without `{flag}`: stdout and the exit code are identical, and only the flagged run prints `[{tool_name}]` lines on stderr.

Add an entry describing `{flag}`.
Callers of `{tool}` ({callers}) keep calling it without `{flag}`; do not change them.

items.text: Never print request bodies, credentials or other user data in diagnostic lines; report names, counts and outcomes only.

items.text: Timing or profiling information for each of the {reported}.
